data.title: Stability concerns have Fed considering dormant capital rule
data.description:
• Key insight: Some Federal Reserve officials are discussing the merits of activating the countercyclical capital buffer — which raises bank capital during the upswing of a business cycle to bolster the banking system during the downswing — for the first time in years. 
  • Expert quote: “The Fed policy framework sets the standard for deploying the countercyclical capital buffer as a period when systemic vulnerabilities are meaningfully above normal. It’s pretty clear that current conditions meet that criteria.” — Jeremy Kress, University of Michigan law professor and former Fed lawyer.

Rising financial stability concerns have some members of the Federal Open Market Committee eying a heretofore unused Federal Reserve regulatory tool.

data.title: How Block is pushing its AI to merchants
data.description:
• Key insights: Block’s merchant payments unit Square launched Squaremates, a business agent that can perform tasks for Square sellers. 
  • What’s at stake: Jack Dorsey’s payments company spent the better part of the last year using artificial intelligence to reimagine how it operates. Now, Block is pushing some of that technology to merchants. 

After more than a year of using artificial intelligence to reshape — and downsize — its organization, Block is providing its sellers with that same technology it hopes will help merchants run their businesses more efficiently.

data.title: Anthropic’s business model is creating a new kind of debt — comprehension debt
data.description:
Dario Amodei, the CEO of newly public Anthropic, said something extraordinary the other day. In explaining what he calls “pacing” in terms of developing the company’s products, he used the metaphor of a car that could drive 200 miles an hour. “We could drive at 200 miles an hour, maybe let’s only drive at 90 miles an hour.”

In other words, the company could develop its products at break-neck speed and release them, but Anthropic has chosen not to do that. Amodei was presenting this as an example of the elevated reasoning at the company.

data.title: Why insurtech unicorn Corgi wants a traditional bank charter
data.description:
• Key insight: Corgi, an insurtech founded two years ago with a focus on AI insurance, has requested a national bank charter in a first for insurers since the Dodd-Frank Act.
  • Expert quote: “Regulators will probe how the firm uses AI and whether it is well-controlled.” -Klaros Group’s Roman Goldstein

AI-powered insurtech startup Corgi is sniffing out a path to a full-service bank charter.

data.title: Costs of running branches in big cities vary widely: Report
data.description:
• Key insight: Location and market conditions largely determine the cost of operating a bank branch, and the difference between certain markets is large, according to a report from JLL, a commercial real estate and investment management firm that manages bank properties.
  • Supporting data: It costs 2.6 times as much money to operate a branch in New York City than it does in Orange County, California, according to JLL’s analysis of 12 U.S. markets.

data.title: Why referrals are bank-based advisors’ best friends and worst enemies
data.description:
• Key insight: Advisors often view the bank channel as a steady source of client referrals. But that source of business has started drying up even as the chances that they’ll be sued if they leave remain strong.
  • Expert quote: “Those customers, they typically have a much much tighter relationship with the bank than they will an FA that’s been assigned to them.” — Ron Edde, founder of Millennium Career Advisors

The very reasons some financial advisors choose to anchor their careers in the bank channel is, perhaps counterintuitively, their biggest impediment to eventually leaving, according to industry data.

data.title: Federal Home Loan bank lending surged 15% in third quarter
data.description:
• Key insight: Third-quarter advances from the Federal Home Loan banks rose 15% to $798.4 million as banks, credit unions and insurers sought liquidity amid higher interest rates. 
  • What’s at stake: With Treasury yields above 5% and deposits moving toward higher-yielding money-market funds, commercial banks continue to tap the Home Loan Bank System to maintain liquidity without broadly repricing deposits.

data.title: TruStage struck a deal with its attacker. What did it buy?
data.description:
• Key insight: TruStage disclosed Thursday that it “came to a resolution” with the attacker behind the July cyberattack on its systems. The attacker promised to destroy any data it took.
  • What’s at stake: Any credit union member data the attacker took is now protected chiefly by a criminal’s promise, and credit unions can’t tell members or regulators anything definitive until TruStage finishes its investigation.

data.title: Fed’s Cook questions whether one rate hike is enough
data.description:
• Key insight: Federal Reserve Gov. Lisa Cook said the current economic climate calls for decisive action to rein in inflation. 
  • Expert quote: “In a different environment, the Committee could afford to be patient, but I continue to believe that in this economic climate we do not have that luxury.” — Federal Reserve Gov. Lisa Cook

Federal Reserve Gov. Lisa Cook expressed doubt Friday that September’s interest rate increase was enough to curb persistently high inflation, warning that the central bank risks falling behind the curve if it waits too long to tighten monetary policy further.

data.title: Press Release Brazil’s Daycoval Selects Temenos SaaS to Power its US Expansion
data.description:
Temenos (SIX: TEMN), a global leader in banking technology, today announced that Banco Daycoval S.A. (Daycoval), a major Brazilian bank specializing in corporate lending, has selected Temenos SaaS on Microsoft Azure to drive its international expansion in the United States.

Daycoval will initially adopt services including core banking, digital onboarding and financial crime mitigation on Temenos SaaS, later adding payments and trade finance capabilities, as the bank seeks to better support its corporate clients operating internationally.

Ranked among Brazil’s top 20 banks by total assets, Daycoval is a well-established and diversified financial institution with a nationwide presence and a comprehensive range of financial products and services. The bank combines its core business of lending to companies with selected retail banking activities, while steadily expanding its presence in capital markets and investment banking. 

Founded in 1968, Daycoval has approximately 4,500 employees and in the first nine months of 2026 reported recurring net income of R$1.36 billion and ROAE of 23.8%.  Its expanded loan portfolio reached R$80.1 billion at the end of September, up 24.4% YoY, while total funding stood at R$80.2 billion. Asset quality remained sound, with a 90-day NPL ratio at 2.2%. Additionally, the Bank’s Basel Capital Ratio increased 150bps QoQ to 14.3%.

Daycoval already has an international presence through its branch in the Cayman Islands and recently received conditional approval to open a federal branch in the United States. Through the new branch, Daycoval initially plans to offer corporate deposit accounts, bilateral and external lending, and domestic and international payments, further strengthening its offering for corporate clients engaged in international business, particularly those seeking to expand in the United States.

With Temenos SaaS, Daycoval will benefit from a comprehensive set of banking services, including capabilities tailored to the needs of the US market, delivered on a single platform that will help the bank reduce integration risk. Temenos’ flexible, cloud-native solution will enable Daycoval to scale efficiently and add new capabilities progressively as its US operations expand.

Adopting a SaaS model, with updates, support and maintenance handled by Temenos, will empower Daycoval to focus on its customers, rather than on managing its technology. Meanwhile, Temenos’ open, API-based architecture will enable seamless integration with other bank systems and third-party solutions, helping it to launch new products rapidly and deliver an enhanced digital experience. 

Paulo Saba, Investor Relations Senior Officer, Banco Daycoval S.A., said: “Establishing a branch in the United States is a key pillar of our international expansion strategy, enabling Daycoval to better support the international operations of our longstanding clients”. 

Marta Alves, General Manager, Banco Daycoval S.A. (Miami Branch), added “Temenos’ proven capabilities and flexible, cloud-native platform will enable us to establish our US presence quickly and scale efficiently as our business evolves, supporting disciplined and sustainable growth.”

Rodrigo Silva, President, Latin America, Temenos said: “We’re delighted that Daycoval has chosen Temenos SaaS for its expansion into the US. This is a clear vote of confidence in Temenos’ capabilities for the US market, as well as further evidence of our growing momentum in Brazil. We look forward to helping Daycoval to meet the evolving needs of its international corporate clients with agility and speed on Temenos SaaS.”

data.title: BankThink Washington could learn a lot from Europe on crypto regulation
data.description:
• Key insight: Unlike in the U.S., where the crypto industry has endured regulation-by-enforcement for most of a decade, Europe has made real strides toward a rules-based order. Policymakers in Washington should take note.
  • Forward look: Washington should not read Europe’s experience simply as a cautionary tale about overregulation. The U.S. could be seen as a cautionary tale for under-regulating, which has led to regulation by enforcement for over a decade, encouraging legitimate businesses to stay offshore.

Europe gets a bad rap in tech. The “regulate rather than innovate” criticism has become so overused that it’s nearly meaningless. And while it’s true that Europe has slower growth than America, there are certain areas where regulation makes sense.
